scope.plan: docs/work-plans/golden-delivery-planning.md: Next RM-403 response-bound slice — short plan, review before implementation
scope.purpose: Assess finite caller-visible readiness response under the existing one-second monotonic budget while retaining one native probe/recovery attempt until settlement, preventing late ready/client publication, and preserving startup/fatal semantics.
scope.mode: Read-only plan/source checks; no implementation, compiler build, runtime probe or test execution.

human_option_clarification.accepted_option: Compiler-private bundled controller with one attempt-owned responsePromise/deadlineAt and distinct nativePending state; once-only publication after activeAttempt identity, strict monotonic deadline and fatal fence. Timeout resolves false, marks not-ready and advances backoff once while retaining the native slot; later callers join the already-resolved false response. Recovery calls initializePersistenceOnce(false), startup defaults to true, and construction/rebinding is owned by a valid publication callback.
human_option_clarification.disposition: Suitable concrete implementation option; no additional owner decision required for this response-bound slice.
necessary_distinctions: Do not overload settled: responseSettled and nativeSettled/nativePending have different lifetimes. Slot release follows the aggregate native initializer/probe promise, never responsePromise settlement.
The one-second budget belongs to the attempt. A later caller has only the remaining budget or immediately receives false after expiry; no fresh per-caller second, timer or raw-native race is needed.

initializePersistenceOnce(false) suppresses the complete successful publication at target.rs:3432, including ready, probe-needed/reporting/fatal reset effects. Its genuine unavailable/fatal failure classification remains active. The default true startup path retains prior behavior.

A candidate may be constructed only after passing the success fence, then the fence is rechecked before actual rebinding/publication if construction can consume time. No await between final check and state publication.
An attempt-level timer cannot establish a hard response bound if synchronous SQLite, an event-loop stall or synchronous cancellation blocks progress; those limitations remain explicit.

contract_assessment.accepted: CONFIG-D10/CONFIG-P5 require bounded, secret-safe readiness, local dependency-free liveness, bounded attempt concurrency/backoff and recovery without restart. TIME-D06 requires monotonic deadlines. The saved slice implements a response budget without pretending a timer interrupts native work. Keeping an expired attempt resident until settlement satisfies native attempt concurrency; a permanently stalled native attempt therefore stays not-ready rather than starting replacement attempts.
contract_assessment.original_failure_preserved: The original independent review observed 32 stalled probe requests, one probe, one noop cancel and zero settled responses at logical t=60000; pending initialization similarly had one attempt, no timer and zero settled requests. These remain original evidence, not new measurements. The saved plan directly addresses both unresolved response paths. No historical review, failure or raw result was rewritten.

contract_assessment.approval_meaning: The plan's accepted semantics and scope are sound. The concrete implementation must satisfy the refinements below; this is not evidence that those algorithms already exist or that RM-403 is complete.

required_implementation_constraints.requirement: One attempt-owned bounded response and one separately observed native completion.
required_implementation_constraints.algorithm: Install the attempt record in the single-flight slot synchronously before invoking any dependency callback. Each attempt owns one monotonic deadline, one timer, one deferred boolean response and one native-completion observer with explicit fulfillment/rejection handlers. Calls joining a live attempt reuse its bounded response. Once expired, return false immediately even after the retry cutoff passes; do not register more reactions or timers against the unresolved native promise. Only actual native/aggregate initialization settlement releases the slot, guarded by exact attempt identity.
required_implementation_constraints.avoid: Per-request Promise.race(rawAttempt, timeout), per-request rawAttempt.finally, clearing the slot when the response settles, or spawning a background retry while the native attempt is still pending. Repeated races against a never-settling promise accumulate reactions even if each HTTP response returns. Ensure ignored promises derived from completion observers cannot reject unhandled.

required_implementation_constraints.requirement: Expire caller response independently of cancellation and keep timeout failure sticky.
required_implementation_constraints.algorithm: At deadline, set expired first, publish persistenceReady=false, settle the shared response false and account failure/backoff once. Any best-effort cancel request is guarded, caught and cannot be awaited as a prerequisite to answering. A thrown/noop/ineffective cancel must not strand callers, erase failure state or release the native slot. Settle/cleanup paths must be idempotent.
required_implementation_constraints.limit: A timer and cancellation call cannot bound an event-loop-blocking native/synchronous call. The budget means a scheduler-governed async response deadline, not a platform-independent one-second wall-clock guarantee.

required_implementation_constraints.requirement: Commit success only through an identity/deadline/fatal fence, checked at publication time.
required_implementation_constraints.algorithm: After full probe or schema/authentication completion, require the active slot to be this attempt, expired=false, monotonic now strictly less than deadlineAt, and fatal=false. Prepare any replacement client, then recheck immediately before one synchronous publication block with no await between check and commit. The timer callback alone is insufficient: fulfillment arriving after the deadline can run before a delayed timer callback. Equality at the deadline fails closed. Late healthy completion and late init completion may release the slot but cannot set ready, clear fatal/timeout evidence, refresh healthy cache or replace the active client.
required_implementation_constraints.fresh_failure_note: Do not clear availability evidence raised after the attempt began merely because an older probe succeeded. If such concurrent invalidation is possible, fence publication using a captured invalidation generation or equivalent dirty-state comparison; never use an old success to erase a newer probe-needed event.

required_implementation_constraints.requirement: Recovery initialization must stage its result without pre-publishing ready or bypassing the response fence.
required_implementation_constraints.algorithm: Separate schema/native work from the successful initialization publication at target.rs:3432. initializePersistenceOnce(publish=true) is a suitable per-call private option: false suppresses all success-state publication, while default true preserves startup. The recovery controller owns ready/client/cache publication. Preserve handle ownership, including the authentication initializer's handles, and do not close or swap a handle still used by unsettled native work. The existing finite sequential schema/authentication chain may remain one owned recovery attempt until its aggregate native completion; do not release the slot early or detach native operations. Optionally add a private validity check before dispatching further schema work after an await to stop expired work sooner. This optimization is not required to prove the accepted caller-response/one-attempt invariant and cannot pretend to roll back already dispatched work.
required_implementation_constraints.safe_api_options: Use the clarified per-call publish boolean, or a compiler-private initializePersistenceNative(context?) -> InitOutcome with an existing-semantics startup wrapper. Explicit typed outcome or separate retained error classification can preserve fatal/unavailable distinctions. Thread captured handles/private context through initializeAuthenticationStorage only if needed by the chosen ownership or early-stop design. Avoid a globally mutable publication mode or authored capability/configuration bypass.

required_implementation_constraints.requirement: Preserve actual fatal classification, including after caller timeout; do not turn synthetic expiry into schema corruption.
required_implementation_constraints.algorithm: Use distinct outcomes such as ok, unavailable, fatal and expired. A timeout/control-fence result is unavailable for the response, not an arbitrary Error that falls into the current fatal initializer branch. Preserve the reviewed SQLite BUSY/LOCKED initialization recovery classification. A real incompatible schema/configuration failure discovered when an expired native operation rejects must still set the fatal latch and retain safe diagnostic reporting; success fencing must not suppress genuine fatal evidence. Once latched, a late success or timeout cleanup cannot clear fatal state. Future readiness remains false with no retry when fatal.
required_implementation_constraints.startup: Retain typed configuration validation and incompatible schema/authentication rejection before binding. Do not race the top-level startup initializer or open the listener early in this slice.

required_implementation_constraints.requirement: Advance retry backoff once per failed attempt, independently of request count or late settlement.
required_implementation_constraints.algorithm: Reuse 250ms initial delay, doubling to the existing 5000ms cap. Record nextAttemptAt from the one logical failure/expiry event, never from every waiter. A late retryable rejection or success cannot count a second failure or reset backoff. Retry requires both native settlement and monotonic cutoff eligibility; if cutoff elapsed while the native attempt stayed pending, the next eligible request may start one new attempt after settlement. Early fenced success resets delay to 250ms and establishes the one-second healthy cache. Expired attempts never establish healthy cache. Preserve allowed mixed per-request 200/503 results across recovery cutoffs; do not impose an atomic 32-request snapshot.

suggested_private_controller_shape.attempt: { identity, deadlineAt, expired, outcomeRecorded, response: Promise<boolean>, settleResponse, timer, nativeSettled }
suggested_private_controller_shape.start: Reserve slot -> install one deadline timer -> invoke native work with captured handles/context -> attach exactly one handled completion observer.
suggested_private_controller_shape.caller: Fatal -> false; expired resident attempt -> false; live resident attempt -> shared response; otherwise apply healthy-cache/retry-cutoff eligibility and start at most one attempt.
suggested_private_controller_shape.deadline: Expire and settle false -> publish not-ready -> account failure once -> best-effort cancel without dependence on cancel settlement.
suggested_private_controller_shape.native_completion: Classify real failure, preserving fatal evidence -> fence any success publication -> resolve response if still pending -> clear timer -> release only the matching native-settled slot. Never await native cleanup on the HTTP response path or drop ownership of ongoing native work.
suggested_private_controller_shape.test_seams: Inject compiler-private now/schedule/clear and dependency callbacks into an extracted/generated controller for host tests. Production fixes the real functions; authored Jadpo cannot access or override these seams. This is an API proposal, not implemented code.

required_future_evidence: Unsettled native probe with noop cancel: 32 concurrent callers resolve false at the one shared deadline; later request waves resolve false immediately; native attempts, timer installations and native completion observers remain one regardless of request count or elapsed retry cutoffs.

Unsettled recovery initialization: same finite response and resident-slot assertions; no ready flag or client publication before the controller fence. The whole sequential initializer remains owned through actual completion; if an early-stop fence is added, an expired early operation must not dispatch subsequent steps when it settles.

Native success just before deadline commits once; success exactly at or after deadline fails closed even if timer callback is delayed; no timeout can overturn an already committed eligible success for a different attempt.

Late probe/init success never publishes ready, swaps the active client, resets backoff or refreshes healthy cache. Late rejection is handled without unhandled rejection, double accounting or slot overlap. Include fatal late rejection and synthetic expiry not latching fatal.
Throwing cancellation and synchronously throwing dependency startup resolve safely; no abandoned slot/timer and no cancellation-per-request amplification.

Retry cutoff boundary and doubling/cap remain correct; no new attempt while native work is resident, exactly one new attempt once settled and eligible; eventual fresh success restores readiness and client once. Retain mixed-batch-safe assertions.

Generated handler uses the bounded response, expiry clears ordinary-traffic readiness, liveness remains dependency-free, and ready/not-ready status/body remain consistent and secret-safe. Pair future controlled promise tests with separately reviewed real PostgreSQL connection recovery and current generated-source correspondence.

Preserve startup invalid configuration/incompatible authentication schema rejection and transient SQLite initialization lock recovery. Keep sync blocking, native cleanup and whole startup latency limits explicitly open.
